clue.text: Skilful, confining English to a rout

indicators.note: confining means holding something within, so the skilful word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: skilful means deft

explanation.surface: A deft player, hemming in an English side, crushes them.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a crushing loss, a synonym for a heavy beating suffered in battle or sport.

clue.text: It's rased in storm or other catastrophe

indicators.note: being caught in a storm throws the letters about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something razed to the ground in a storm or some other disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in storm' rearranges the eight letters of IT'S RASED; 'or other' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe is a calamity, the same as a disaster.

clue.text: Source of warmth is thick coat, new one

parts.note: an animal's thick coat is its fur
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A heavy fur coat, a new one, will keep you warm.
explanation.definitionFit: A furnace is an enclosed fire that heats a building, so it supplies warmth.

clue.text: Aircraft instrument to change covering a period

indicators.note: covering means lying over and around, so the word for change surrounds the period

parts.note: to change is to alter
a period of hours or years is time

explanation.surface: A pilot's gauge used to modify flight over a stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: An altimeter is the gauge in a cockpit that shows height above the ground.

clue.text: Ancient civilization isn't represented at back of incomplete maps

indicators.note: at back of places the rearranged letters after the shortened book
incomplete means the word for a book of maps loses its last letter

parts.note: a book of maps is an atlas

indicators.note: represented means presented in a new form, so the letters of isn't are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lost ancient city missing from the back of an unfinished set of maps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts ATLAS to ATLA; 'represented' rearranges ISNT to NTIS, which 'at back of' puts after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantis is the legendary island civilization said to have sunk beneath the sea.

clue.text: Vermin controlled by docker?

parts.note: a docker here is someone who docks tails, as the farmer's wife does with a carving knife to the trio of sightless rodents in the nursery rhyme

explanation.walkthrough: A docker is normally a dock worker; here it is one who docks (cuts off) tails, as the farmer's wife does in the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cuts off the tails of the three sightless mice, controlling those rodents.

clue.text: A second complete collection is a valuable item

parts.note: a complete collection of things is a set

explanation.surface: Owning one more full set makes a prized possession.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is something of worth that a person or firm owns.

clue.text: Part of rigging, raised a little, to feel wrong

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, so in a down clue the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a spot is a little amount, as in a spot of tea
to ail is to feel unwell

explanation.surface: A sailor, hauled up a little way into the rigging, starts feeling ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns SPOT upwards into TOPS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A topsail is a sail set above the lowest sail on a mast, part of a ship's rig.

clue.text: Slim second volume's the best, if one's skipping

parts.note: V is the standard abbreviation for volume

indicators.note: skipping means leaving out, so the word for the best drops a letter

parts.note: the elite are the best
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A second slim book is the finest, provided one skips parts of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skipping' takes I (one) from ELITE, leaving ELTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Svelte means slender and graceful, a synonym for slim.

clue.text: Vehicles set alight in film

definitions.meaning: horse-drawn war carts burning, so carts that are aflame
the 1981 British Oscar-winning film about Olympic runners

explanation.surface: Burning carriages appear in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the title describes burning war carriages; it is also the name of a 1981 film about athletes at the 1924 Olympics.

clue.text: It extends support for medical emergencies

definitions.meaning: something that extends or lengthens things, a device that pulls them out
a frame on which an injured person is carried

explanation.surface: Something that lengthens things also carries casualties.
explanation.definitionFit: One that makes things longer is literally a thing that stretches; it is also the litter used to carry the injured.

clue.text: Composer cutting short meal

indicators.note: cutting short means trimming the end, so the word for the meal loses its last letter

parts.note: an evening meal is supper

explanation.surface: A composer cuts dinner short.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz von Suppé was a 19th-century Austrian composer of operettas.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz von Suppé wrote operettas and overtures such as Light Cavalry, so he is a composer.

clue.text: Problem leading to start of speech being repeated

definitions.text: Problem leading to start of speech being repeated

parts.words: Problem leading to start of speech being repeated
parts.note: a speech disorder in which the opening sounds of words come out again and again

explanation.definitionFit: A stutter is a speech impediment in which initial sounds are repeated involuntarily.

clue.text: Competitor, in the event, ran third

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the clue's words, running across event, ran and third

explanation.surface: A runner in the race came third.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters running from evENT through RAN to the T of Third.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrant is someone who has entered a contest, a competitor.

clue.text: Calm, then tense? It happens

parts.note: calm means even, as in an even temper
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: First composed, then nervous: a description of a mood swing.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence, something that takes place.

clue.text: Line in translation of Fidelio? It's rigged

indicators.note: in means the line letter is placed inside the rearranged opera title
translation of means turning into another form, so the letters of Fidelio are reworked

explanation.surface: A line in a version of Beethoven's opera Fidelio seems to be fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation of' rearranges FIDELIO, and 'in' puts L inside. 'rigged' looks like 'fixed' but means fitted with drilling rigs.
explanation.definitionFit: An area where crude is extracted is covered with drilling rigs, hence fairly said to be rigged.

clue.text: Fashionable military leader is not particular

parts.note: fashionable means in, as in the in thing
a general is a senior military leader

explanation.surface: A trendy army commander isn't fussy.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking broadly, rather than of specific cases, means not dealing with particulars.

clue.text: Article's attempt to capture church's history

indicators.note: to capture means to take inside, so the article and attempt hold the church letters

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, here with its s
CE is the Church of England
an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: A newspaper article tries to cover a church's past.
explanation.walkthrough: AN'S plus TRY gives ANSTRY; 'to capture' puts CE inside, after the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry is family lineage, one's line of descent, so a personal history.

clue.text: Jail is prepared after one politician's end in dishonour

indicators.note: after means the words is prepared come after the rest

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: end in means the last letter of the next word

parts.note: on can mean ready, as in 'are you on?' meaning ready to go ahead

explanation.surface: A gaol is ready for a politician who ends in disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end in' takes R from dishonour; 'after' places IS ON (is prepared) after I, MP and R.
explanation.definitionFit: To jail someone is to lock them up, the verb meaning confine in a cell.

clue.text: Family of writers with German, supporting Germany

parts.note: mit is German for with
supporting means for, as in for the motion
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A literary family with German roots who back Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mitford sisters, such as Nancy and Jessica, were a famous English family of writers, and some backed Nazi Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Nancy, Jessica and Diana were the best-known of the six aristocratic sisters, several of them authors.

clue.text: Board to show greater antiquity

definitions.meaning: to board a bus or train is to climb aboard it
to grow older, as in 'he's getting on a bit'

explanation.surface: Climbing aboard to display one's advanced age.
explanation.definitionFit: Boarding a vehicle is climbing on; growing old is advancing in years, both the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: One steals leftover bit of drink

definitions.meaning: a thief, in Cockney rhyming slang
a scrap left in the bottom of a cuppa

explanation.surface: A thief pockets the dregs of someone's cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang makes a thief a tea-leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang a robber is a tea-leaf, and literally it is the fragment left at the bottom of a cup.

clue.text: A bomb going up, trapping Government, is a mystery

indicators.note: trapping means holding inside, so the reversed pair surrounds the government letter
going up means read bottom to top in a down clue

parts.note: a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: An explosion rising and catching the government is puzzling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns A MINE into ENIMA; 'trapping' then holds G inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a puzzle, a riddle or something baffling.

clue.text: A pint? Absolutely!

definitions.meaning: a pint is twice a half-pint, so it is a full measure

explanation.surface: Fancy a pint? I certainly do!
explanation.walkthrough: British pubs serve beer in pints and halves; 'not half!' is British slang meaning 'definitely'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint is a full measure rather than a half, and the British exclamation means 'very much so'.

clue.text: Minister offering no opening for crime

indicators.note: offering no opening means the first letter of the minister's word is dropped

parts.note: a parson is a minister of the church

explanation.surface: A clergyman with nothing to say for himself is a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the offence of setting fire to property on purpose.

clue.text: Collection of pictures depicting time on French peak

indicators.note: on means the time word comes next to and after the peak in this across clue

parts.note: mont is French for mountain
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Pictures showing a moment on an Alpine summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A montage is a composite made of several images combined.

clue.text: Good area of Scotland? That's outrageous

parts.note: Ross is a region of the Scottish Highlands

explanation.surface: A Scottish place is fine? How shocking!
explanation.walkthrough: Ross is a historic district in the north of Scotland, part of Ross and Cromarty.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross means flagrant or glaring, as in gross negligence, a synonym for scandalous.

clue.text: Briefly including Rector's wrong, wrong

parts.note: inc. is the short form of including

indicators.note: wrong means not right, so the letters of rector are put in a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: In short, the rector is in error, quite wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'wrong' rearranges RECTOR to ORRECT; the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Incorrect means mistaken or untrue, a synonym for erroneous.

clue.text: French area Andersen represented

indicators.note: represented means shown in a new form, so the letters of Andersen are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hans Christian Andersen portrayed a region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ardennes is a forested upland region spanning north-east France, Belgium and Luxembourg.

clue.text: Very furry hare taking in expert? Not at first

indicators.note: taking in means holding inside, so the word for hare surrounds the shortened expert

parts.note: to hare is to run fast, to fly

indicators.note: not at first means the expert's word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a buff is an expert or enthusiast

explanation.surface: A very hairy hare swallows a specialist, but not at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hare' is a verb, to rush, so FLY; 'Not at first' cuts BUFF to UFF, which 'taking in' puts inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluffy means covered in soft down, as in a fluffy kitten, so very furry.
